subject.title: [Bug]: Codex app-server session wedges indefinitely after a 429 rate-limit burst — terminal-idle watchdog still gated by `activeAppServerTurnRequests > 0` (regression/incomplete fix of #82681)

question: Should this issue close now based on current-main source proof from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102160, or stay open until live 429 confirmation is posted from a release containing that PR?
rationale: The source and tests show a plausible current-main structural fix, but the latest human discussion explicitly asked to keep the issue open until release-level live 429 confirmation, and the fix is not in v2026.6.11.

options.title: Keep Open For Live 429 Proof
options.body: Leave this issue open until a release with the run-lifecycle stack proves the shared Codex app-server no longer wedges multiple sessions past completion idle.

options.title: Close As Current-Main Fixed
options.body: Close now as implemented by the merged run-lifecycle stack, accepting source and regression-test proof without a live 429 reproduction.

options.title: Split Remaining Timeout Work
options.body: Treat the shared-client wedge as fixed by the merged stack and move only terminal-idle timeout configurability or wording to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/85242.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Live 429 Proof
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open until a release with the run-lifecycle stack proves the shared Codex app-server no longer wedges multiple sessions past completion idle.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged reliability stack and the latest status comment setting the live-confirmation condition.
